newsitem.title: USA: Centennial restates earnings to show losses.
newsitem.headline: Centennial restates earnings to show losses.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc., whose founder is in jail on charges of insider trading, restated its earnings Thursday for almost four years to show losses instead of profits.
The Wilmington, Mass.-based maker of computer memory cards said its previous sales figures were allegedly inflated by its former founder and chief executive, Emanuel Pinez.
Pinez, who has been charged by the Securities and Exchange Commission with insider trading, has denied any wrongdoing.
As a result of the alleged mismanagement, Centennial's stock was delisted in March, its chief financial officer was fired and several class-action suits have been filed against the firm.

Centennial, the best-performing stock on the Big Board last year, reported cumulative losses of $34.5 million for the previous 3-3/4 years ended March 31. The company had previously reported profits of $12.1 million over the period ended on Dec. 31, 1996.
"We really believe we have fixed everything that needs to be fixed," Centennial Treasurer Donald Peck told Reuters.
In its third quarter ended March 31, Centennial actually had a profit of $52,000 before interest and special charges, its first profit since its initial public offering in 1994.
"We have not lost one customer throughout this process, and they are the people who know our product best," Peck said.
Centennial expects to file financial reports by the end of the month, the first substantive step towards the relisting of its common stock on a major exchange, Peck said.

Separately, Centennial said it has received a proposal from Congress Financial, an asset-based lending institution, for new borrowing facilities. Although no binding commitment has been received, Centennial said it expects to have such facilities in place by early July.
The company said its current financing arrangements with First National Bank of Boston are due to expire on June 30, unless extended.
The company said it has its revolving credit loan balance has fallen from about $13.5 million on Feb. 11 to about $5.4 million.
